title: Etale henselian restriction in degree zero
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $Y\to S$ a proper morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $Y_0=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and let $i:Y_0\to Y$ be the canonical closed immersion. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $Y$, restriction along $i$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is an isomorphism $\Gamma(Y,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(Y_0,i^{-1}_{\mathrm{et}}F)$. The isomorphism is natural in $F$, in finite pullback, and in morphisms of henselian pairs.

proof.text: Properness gives compactness and quasi-separatedness of Y. The quotient spectrum map is a closed immersion, and the pullback square makes i a closed immersion. The pullback image formula and the range of the quotient spectrum map give range(i)=p⁻¹(V(I)). The quotient map is surjective, so the affine characterization of closed immersions applies. Prime ideals of A/I correspond to primes of A containing I. The fibre-product point description then gives the image equality, since the tensor product of the two residue fields over their common residue field is nonzero.

For every finite q:X′→Y and irreducible closed C, apply Stein connectedness to q≫p; rewriting range(i) as p⁻¹(V(I)) identifies the resulting connected intersection with C∩q⁻¹(range(i)). The finite-cover connectedness criterion then gives the required module-section isomorphism.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For every etale abelian sheaf $F$ on $X$, restriction induces
$\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X_0,F_0)$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
The canonical map from the etale to Zariski restriction is injective on
stalks because a geometric point has a strictly local etale neighbourhood.
For surjectivity, lift a fibre section etale-locally; quasi-compactness of
$X_0$ gives finitely many local lifts, and Lemma
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-refinement-etale-cover] gives a finite surjective
refinement on which all lifts exist.
The two lifts agree on the finite overlap after restriction to $X_0$ by the
Zariski result, and the equalizer sheaf descends the lift to $X$. Uniqueness
is stalkwise injectivity. The finite-pullback compatibility required in
Stacks Tag `09ZF` is recorded as four explicit equalities:
identity pullback preserves the lift, composition of finite pullbacks preserves
the lift, restriction to $X_0$ recovers the given section, and the descended
section pulls back to each local lift; these are the four preceding lemmas.
The finite refinement lemma proves existence and finite-presentation stage,
and its stalkwise equalizer argument proves equality of the local lifts on
the self-intersection. Thus the four finite-pullback compatibilities
complete the descent.
